name: Abide
reason: Health-restore re-check (12 Nov 2026), new rule: still out. abide.com's home page (robots.txt open, read 12 Nov 2026) answers 'What are the benefits of Christian meditation?' with survey claims that 91% of users 'with mild to chronic depression saw an improvement in their symptoms' and 80% 'with mild to chronic insomnia' slept better, and features a user quote saying Christian meditation let them 'avoid using medication to induce sleep'. That is a claim to treat medical conditions plus an indirect 'instead of medication' message, made in the app's main marketing rather than in one item, so the test ('in unless their pages claim to cure or treat a disease or to replace medical care') puts it out. The content itself (biblical meditations, sleep stories, audio Bible; Guideposts; $39.99/yr after a 7-day trial; help form at help.abide.com) would otherwise suit an App listing on Calm-style terms, so the owner may override if the survey lines are read as user reports rather than claims. Earlier record: this file's previous version (night sprint rank 67).
